original_question: Is every complemented subspace of C[0,1] isomorphic to C(K) for some closed subset K of [0,1]?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 9, the Complemented Subspace Problem for C[0,1]. This is the exact open problem your draft is trying to capture. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=646d208f31321fe467b685afc0b97665b5f04a31&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official formulation almost verbatim: it asks about complemented subspaces of C[0,1], keeps the classification up to isomorphism, and retains the paper’s specific target class C(K) for some closed subset K of [0,1], rather than broadening to a neighboring operator-theoretic or general C(K)-space problem. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=646d208f31321fe467b685afc0b97665b5f04a31&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone formulation, expand the notation C[0,1] to C([0,1]) and specify that C(K) means the Banach space of scalar-valued continuous functions on K with the supremum norm; the paper leaves this under its standard Banach-space notation conventions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))

Make explicit that a complemented subspace means a closed subspace that is the range of a bounded projection on C([0,1]); this is standard but implicit in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.2668))

Make explicit that isomorphic means isomorphic as Banach spaces. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=646d208f31321fe467b685afc0b97665b5f04a31&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Do not broaden the target to an arbitrary compact metric space K: the paper states the closed-subset-of-[0,1] version, and your refinement should stay that narrow. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=646d208f31321fe467b685afc0b97665b5f04a31&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let X be a complemented subspace of the classical Banach space C([0,1]) of scalar-valued continuous functions on [0,1] with the supremum norm. Must X be isomorphic, as a Banach space, to C(K) for some closed subset K of [0,1]? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=646d208f31321fe467b685afc0b97665b5f04a31&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: Section 7 opens by identifying the issue as the classification, up to isomorphism, of all complemented subspaces of C[0,1], and then states Problem 9 in essentially the same form as your draft. The nearby context records the strongest partial result cited there: Rosenthal’s theorem that every complemented subspace of C[0,1] with non-separable dual is isomorphic to C[0,1], obtained via Theorem 6 about operators whose dual has non-separable range fixing a copy of C[0,1]. Problem 10 is then presented as a separate operator-theoretic question motivated by Problem 9 and Theorem 6, not as an equivalent reformulation of Problem 9. So the faithful refinement is simply Problem 9 with the standard Banach-space terminology made explicit, and no alternate formulation should be supplied. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=646d208f31321fe467b685afc0b97665b5f04a31&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
